brief: Goldman's Tony Pasquariello says risk/reward skews positive into year-end. A hedge-fund degross left net exposure at the 3rd percentile, the last seven weeks of the year are seasonally up 69% of the time since 1952 (averaging a 2.1% rally), AI demand looks insatiable per TSMC and CoreWeave's beat-and-raise (though CoreWeave guided to a $1.1 billion quarterly interest bill on $47 billion of debt), and nominal GDP growth is running above trend and accelerating. This holds despite Nvidia losing its only CEO, a third straight hot core CPI print, and the 2-year's worst week in two years, yet the Nasdaq 100 rallied 3.5%. For 2027 he turns cautious: the AI buildout's upside is priced and its uninterrupted path is now at risk from regulation, core CPI is broadening, and bull markets die when the Fed chokes off liquidity, not from old age. Waller floated a 50bp hike, Goldman's economists added a third hike to their forecast, and 2027 brings the largest net Treasury supply increase since 2000. He now calls the setup a 'seesaw,' not last week's 'turn.' Zero Hedge, relaying the note, argues the seesaw framing understates the risk: the Fed, not the seesaw, will decide 2027, given the economy's reliance on stock-market wealth effects.
